kiln_p18_001.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_001.text: On the first morning of the twenty-ninth week, Yue arrived at the comparison room wearing the new ordinary shoes she had bought with her wages. Zhu had praised them as almost respectable. Luo looked at the sole and asked her to perform the dry posterior stance before discussing respectability. The heel sat differently on the marked block. The inward contact seemed familiar until the outward return drifted. Yue took the shoes off and discovered that purchasing comfort did not purchase an unchanged task. They revised the support height in the cold setup and admitted no personal input that morning.

kiln_p18_002.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_002.text: She carried the shoes upstairs and found Jian mending his own sole. He asked whether she had finally defeated a dangerous piece of footwear. 'It has demanded a formal review,' she said. He lifted his patched shoe solemnly. 'Mine has been operating outside its original specification for years.' She laughed, then explained the actual changed stance. He listened with the pleasure he once took in mechanisms before shame filled every question. Ordinary wear could change a comparison without anyone behaving badly. They went down to breakfast, both stepping more thoughtfully than the cook considered necessary.

kiln_p18_003.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_003.text: The next recovered task used the checked support and the same posterior eighth input over four ordinary breaths. Its inward heel-calf-hip contact and outward return completed cleanly. Luo changed the dry naming order afterward, asking her to distinguish it from the established anterior pair without drawing an imagined full leg circuit. She did so slowly, one contact at a time. The receiver showed the short passage, and the grounded release emptied it. The useful quarter-unit task remained unattempted. Yue had gained something harder to boast about: a clean result after correcting an ordinary change she had wanted to ignore.

kiln_p18_004.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_004.text: Her next-day touch, grip and leg movement remained normal. On another recovered day Luo allowed the quarter input over four ordinary breaths, no more than a sixteenth in one breath. The guarded receiver was set for an eighth useful unit, below the final task. Yue watched its weight shift and tried not to follow the pleasant motion by increasing the next breath. The outward return stayed distinct and interrupted cleanly on the separate check. After full grounded release she rested before any other route. Luo recorded the actual task and said they would see what tomorrow knew about it.

kiln_p18_005.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_005.text: Tomorrow knew that her calf felt oddly awake on the stairs, though ordinary touch and movement were normal. She described the sensation before the scheduled task. Luo deferred additional posterior input and asked the clinician to distinguish ordinary muscular fatigue from a new adverse change. The clinician found no deficit, advised rest and requested a following check. Yue hated how quickly a pleasing result had acquired another blank day. Zhu offered her a chair beside the glaze bench. 'You can still criticize colors sitting down,' she said. Yue sat, relieved to be useful without proving that every sensation was harmless.

kiln_p18_006.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_006.text: The sensation settled after the ordinary rest, with the following movement check normal. Luo repeated the lower quarter-input task only on a separate recovered day, observing the stance and independent interruption. The eighth useful unit moved without the earlier lingering calf sensation. Yue didn't ask for the half input immediately. She wrote the difference between the two days and waited for another following check. The room's slow rhythm had begun to feel like craft rather than punishment: prepare, attempt, stop, retain, compare. She kept both days' readings on the same page rather than letting the cleaner result replace the other.

kiln_p18_007.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_007.text: Su Yan reviewed the sequence through the circuit messenger and approved continued lower repetitions before any higher step. Her note asked whether Yue could identify the posterior outward return after an arm task and whether the calf felt normal after ordinary work, not only after sitting in the comparison room. Luo scheduled the questions on recovered days rather than add them to an already tiring session. Yue spent the afternoon packing qualified bakery trays at waist height. Her body stayed ordinary under that work. The next day she gave the teacher the full answer, including the hours and rests.

kiln_p18_008.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_008.text: The first mixed dry sequence confused her more than she expected. Luo named the second arm pair, then posterior leg, then anterior leg, with no input admitted. Yue found herself searching for the anterior outward contact when he asked for the posterior return. She stopped and began the map again. 'There is no prize for answering before the question finishes,' he said. She grinned through embarrassment. The distinction became clearer when she described where each inward and outward path ran instead of counting first, second, third, fourth. Names helped the record. The route had to remain distinct beneath the name.

kiln_p18_009.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_009.text: At supper Zhu asked why the new pair was not simply the first leg route going the other direction. Yue drew the anterior foot-knee-hip contacts on one slate and the posterior heel-calf-hip contacts on another, with each pair's inward and outward return. Both already included returning movement. Reversing one could not create the other distinct pair. Zhu examined the drawings and said legs were evidently more troublesome than handles. Jian asked to copy the explanation for the public sample folder. Yue refused that purpose: this was her supervised method record, not a casual instruction sheet for visitors to try.

kiln_p18_010.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_010.text: He accepted the refusal and copied only the plain statement that the four-pair stage required four distinct primary pairs, each with its own inward and outward route. No task instructions or admission sequence went into the public folder. Yue was glad he asked before repurposing the page. His cold course had made source scope a practical habit rather than a phrase he could recite. He still looked resentful when a duty ended exactly at its permitted edge. The resentment no longer always became a proposal to cross it. They discussed the exhibition's ugly sound bowls instead, safer for everybody's vanity.

kiln_p18_011.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_011.text: Luo's summer teaching hours grew crowded as ordinary apprentices returned for delayed assessments. He offered Yue fewer sessions that week rather than squeeze a new posterior trial between two exhausting live demonstrations. She initially heard the change as a loss of priority. Then she watched him rubbing his wrist after checking a shelf and remembered his age as something other than a teacher's impressive history. They kept the actual paid instruction agreement and arranged later hours. Her practice source allowance would last until the revised sessions; she couldn't consume it through unauthorized solitary trials to compensate for his tired day.

kiln_p18_012.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_012.text: Peng asked her to help prepare independent assessment packets for the ordinary learners. Yue separated completed observations, corrected historical credit and tasks still unattempted. One young trimmer wanted his best exercise placed first so the assessor would like him. Peng said the order could be clear without hiding the stop he'd made on the next task. Yue showed him her own posterior blank day after calf sensation. 'That page isn't a trick to look modest,' she said. 'It tells the next teacher what to ask.' He considered this, then attached the full sequence with a sigh that sounded painfully familiar.

kiln_p18_013.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_013.text: Jian's fifth remedial week involved a cold mechanism whose safe stop could be reached only after noticing a changed receiving position. He first answered from the old model's familiar arrangement. The teacher asked him to show the actual receiver. He stopped, identified the change and requested the revised scope before proceeding. The mistake remained in the assessment note beside the correct recovery. Jian brought it to Yue without trying to erase the first answer. He said he hated looking unreliable on paper. She answered that the paper now showed the teacher exactly where he'd become more reliable during the task.

kiln_p18_014.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_014.text: Han had returned to selected warm-room duties, but not the original active hot-grit post. His skin had healed enough for ordinary clothing, while tenderness and the clinician's review still limited exposure and prolonged reaching. He teased everyone for continuing to offer a special chair. Yue asked whether he wanted the chair removed. He said not to be absurd; it was a good chair. Jian laughed before remembering to be careful. Han gave him a dry look. 'If the chair needs a public apology, I'll tell you.' The table relaxed for a minute without pretending the whole winter had left.

kiln_p18_015.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_015.text: The owner received an inquiry from a communal kitchen outside town. Its ordinary bowls broke often under rough handling and harsh cleaning, and it wanted a practical maker to review the use before offering a replacement commission. Tan brought the request to Zhu rather than promise a thousand miraculous bowls. The trimmer wanted the study. Luo wanted the cleaning conditions and broken samples. Peng wanted the failed work retained instead of discarded after the sale. Yue wanted to visit a place where pottery mattered through meals rather than examination. They agreed to a paid preliminary inspection, without production obligation.

kiln_p18_016.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_016.text: The communal kitchen served workers who came and went with the road season. Its caretaker showed Yue a shelf of chipped bowls and a stack of mismatched replacements. 'I would like a bowl nobody throws,' she said. Zhu replied that ceramics could improve the rim but not the thrower. The caretaker laughed and gave her the cleaning brush and solution. One chip came from a heavy pot stacked inside a shallow bowl; another fine crack followed a hot rinse after a cold night. The body sample alone couldn't explain them all. They mapped actual use before discussing the proposed shape.

kiln_p18_017.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_017.text: At the wash bench a worker offered Yue the heaviest basin as a compliment to her cultivation. She chose the lighter measured load within her current physical clearance and asked for a partner on the heavy one. He looked disappointed, as though a rank should be a public performance. Zhu rescued the moment by taking the cleaning brush and saying her own title entitled her to criticize everyone else's rims. The worker laughed and helped lift. Yue appreciated the ordinary diversion. She could decline an untested bodily demand without explaining her whole cultivation method to a stranger.

kiln_p18_018.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_018.text: The kitchen's caretaker asked whether charged ware might keep meals warm longer. Luo explained the additional qualification, source and operating duties such a use would require. Their current inquiry concerned ordinary durable bowls. A thicker ordinary shape and sensible serving sequence might address the immediate need without introducing a new method nobody there could supervise. The caretaker preferred that practical path. Yue noticed her own relief. She wanted to advance, but did not want every useful commission to become an excuse for someone to borrow cultivation's prestige before knowing who would safely operate it after the maker left.

kiln_p18_019.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_019.text: They returned with paid notes, broken pieces and permission to retain samples. The kitchen kept its working stock and received its copies. Zhu designed a rounded rim with a supported ordinary foot, then rejected her first drawing when it nested badly. Jian made the cold spacing model under the assigned teacher. His model showed that the attractive deep shape would trap a cleaning brush between stacked bowls. Yue laughed when Zhu called the model honest. They revised the shape before any production promise. Zhu put the revised drawing in the customer's packet and shook her head at the first mistake.

kiln_p18_020.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_020.text: The preliminary sample body used a retained delivery from the same source as the ordinary schedule. A new clay batch would require its own check; the source name didn't guarantee identical material through every season. Zhu made small comparison pieces for the cleaning and temperature changes the kitchen used. The first rim resisted chipping in the defined ordinary comparison but the foot developed a fine crack after the heating sequence. Luo held that combination. Yue carried the failed piece beneath the stairs and felt an old disappointment become easier to bear when the trial had been meant to find it.

kiln_p18_021.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_021.text: At the archive table she encountered the old apparently sound charged teaching cup again. Its failed guarded release sat beside the kitchen's ordinary thermal crack, each with a different task and result. She imagined how a hurried future reader might call both simply unsuitable ceramics. Peng asked her to draft the new index note. Yue named the body, geometry, process and use before the verdict. The ordinary bowl couldn't be rescued by the cup's charge tests; the cup couldn't be approved because an ordinary bowl survived cleaning. She placed the notes apart and linked only the craft questions they shared.

kiln_p18_022.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_022.text: The kitchen inquiry gave Zhu a reason to walk outside town before the hot afternoon. She took the road slowly, protecting her hand from a swinging tool bag. Yue carried the light copies. At a shaded boundary stone the trimmer stopped to watch a lizard pretend it was part of the wall. 'A successful career,' she said. 'No customer complaints.' Yue asked whether the lizard had qualified its color. Zhu flicked a dry grass stem at her shoe. Their laughter startled the animal into an ungraceful retreat. For once, neither needed the walk to become evidence of improving health.

kiln_p18_023.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_023.text: They reached a small bridge where the river had fallen below its winter mark. Ordinary workers had laid temporary stepping boards for the bank path, with a sign asking visitors to use the bridge for heavy loads. Zhu admired the directness of that instruction. Yue chose the bridge and found it longer by perhaps twenty steps. Twenty steps had once seemed a ridiculous price for a limit. After the shoulder months and the vent account, she paid it easily. Zhu noticed and said nothing. The town looked different when every shortcut no longer felt like a challenge to her competence.

kiln_p18_024.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_024.text: At the communal kitchen, the caretaker introduced the worker who did most of the washing. He wanted bowls that stacked without trapping dirty water, not another elegant shape that made his wrists ache. The current drawing solved one rim problem and created an awkward grip at the foot. Zhu asked him to show the ordinary motion. He did, impatiently at first, then with interest when she changed the cold model. Yue held the drawing board while the new mark went down. Zhu wrote the washer's name beside the correction and asked him to check her drawing.

kiln_p18_025.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_025.text: The washer refused a proposed textured band because residue caught in the grooves. Zhu rubbed her thumb over the model and agreed. The caretaker wanted a mark that distinguished kitchen property from bowls borrowed by road workers. Peng's later note suggested a simple external maker and owner mark away from the cleaning surface. The technical solution was less decorative than Zhu wanted. She accepted it and saved the color idea for a wall tile. Yue admired the separate choices. A maker could keep an artistic ambition alive without forcing every customer to use its first inconvenient expression.

kiln_p18_026.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_026.text: On their return, a cart driver offered them a ride on top of an empty crate stack. Yue declined the unstable perch and negotiated the ordinary seat beside the driver for the stated fare. Zhu complained that sensible travel was making them dull. Then the cart hit a rut and the top crate shifted enough to vindicate dullness. The driver grinned without apologizing for the road. Yue held the light packet and watched the town approach through dust. The next rut threw dust over the packet. Rank might open a route, but a badly secured crate still obeyed ordinary weight.

kiln_p18_027.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_027.text: Back at the hall, Tan asked whether the preliminary visit had produced an attractive sales account. Zhu handed him the washer's notes and said it had produced an unattractive grip correction. He read them and laughed. 'Our specialty continues.' The owner asked about costs, actual prototype hours and the likely ordinary firing slot. No commission was accepted yet. Yue sat through the discussion because she'd witnessed the use, then left before commercial negotiation needed her. She liked participating without pretending participation made every later decision hers. The useful boundary let her go upstairs and rest before the next recovered session.

kiln_p18_028.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_028.text: Jian built two cold stacking models from permitted ordinary materials. One nested neatly and trapped the brush; the other left cleaning access but wasted shelf space. The caretaker would need to choose among actual tradeoffs after seeing the revised version. The boy wanted to declare the second best because the first was plainly wrong. Zhu asked him to list the new drawback too. He frowned, then wrote it. Yue recognized the appeal of an answer that solved a problem so completely nobody could ask another question. Jian wrote the lost shelf space beside the improved cleaning access.

kiln_p18_029.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_029.text: Peng gave the former learners' credit check a quiet afternoon beneath the stairs. She let Yue read one record whose maker had gone into an unrelated trade. The person wanted an accurate history but no present apprenticeship title. Yue had assumed everybody sought the same final qualification Zhu wanted. Peng showed her the letter. 'She wants her work remembered because it happened,' she said. 'Not because she plans to sell it tomorrow.' Yue folded the copy. The archive could serve people who left, not only people who advanced. Her own road ambition began to feel less like abandoning the hall.

kiln_p18_030.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_030.text: Zhu asked the owner for a later paid cold teaching role after her current assessment work. She didn't ask to become a full live-firing teacher whose duties exceeded her hand's limits and unfinished final qualification. The owner offered a trial month designing and teaching specified rim and layout tasks under the existing qualified lead. Zhu would receive credit for her actual instruction design, not disappear behind someone else's signature. Yue saw her friend smiling at the task sheet. An old repaired record mattered. A new fair role mattered differently, because it gave the next month a shape Zhu had chosen.

kiln_p18_031.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_031.text: Zhu's first teaching session went badly. Zhu assumed the learner could already center a shallow bowl, and the rim exercise became a contest with a crooked body. She stopped, paid attention to the prerequisite and revised the sequence. The learner looked ashamed until she admitted her own planning mistake. Jian observed from his permitted cold role and wrote the change in the lesson record. Yue liked seeing Zhu laugh at her first teacher page. Competence at making a rim hadn't automatically supplied competence at explaining one. She revised the next teacher hour and bought a larger cold model.

kiln_p18_032.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_032.text: Afterward Zhu said she'd wanted every pupil to adore the lesson. Yue asked if they had been allowed to criticize it. The trimmer made a face, then added a short feedback question to the next session. One learner asked for a larger cold model; another wanted more time to compare the foot before shaping the rim. The revised lesson improved. Zhu retained both versions and paid Jian for the assigned copying hour through the approved roster. She didn't trade kindness for unpaid assistance. Yue imagined teaching cultivation someday and wrote down the question about prerequisites before vanity could remove it.

kiln_p18_033.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_033.text: Luo watched part of that cold lesson and told Zhu it was useful. She waited for a larger compliment, then decided useful was enough. Later she told Yue the restraint had been heroic. 'I almost demanded that he call it brilliant.' Yue said brilliance might require a separate guarded test. Zhu threw the same clean cloth Yue had missed with and hit the back of her chair. Her good hand remained excellent. They laughed until Peng confiscated the cloth for a task that didn't involve cultivating humility. Zhu retrieved the cloth before Peng could find a dull use for it.

kiln_p18_034.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_034.text: Han returned to the wash bench for a limited warm-room check and found the kitchen models there. He recognized one grip problem from his sister's clinic work. Zhu added his observed note to the comparison without pretending he represented every kitchen. Jian asked him to demonstrate with the uninjured hand, then realized the ordinary task didn't require any demonstration at all; the note and model were enough. Han appreciated the correction. The boy didn't need to make a recovering worker perform for the record. Yue saw the exchange and kept it private because neither had offered it as reconciliation.

kiln_p18_035.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_035.text: Later Han told her he was still angry some mornings. On others he forgot until his sleeve caught a tender place. He disliked being asked whether he'd forgiven Jian more than he disliked the boy's current awkwardness. Yue said she'd stop asking that question in any form. He thanked her. They discussed the new bowls instead, and he insisted a kitchen should use shapes that could survive a tired person's hands. He had become very interested in tired people. Yue remembered the steady long shifts before his injury and asked about the next bowl.

kiln_p18_036.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_036.text: The clinician's next shoulder review included a controlled carry with a partner and a slower lowering movement. Yue completed it without pain or compensating twist. The clinician extended her ordinary waist-height work clearance and kept sudden overhead catching outside the current scope. Yue asked whether that final restriction meant permanent damage. No such finding existed; it meant the movement had not yet been safely reassessed. She accepted the answer and went back to the comparison room with the actual note. A blank permission was different from a dark prophecy, though both could look frightening when she was impatient.

kiln_p18_037.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_037.text: The new note helped Luo separate physical posture from route behavior. He asked Yue to stand in the corrected dry setup and describe where the old protective shoulder habit entered her balance. She could now feel the slight turn before it reached the leg contacts. They worked without input until the movement was comfortable and ordinary. The subsequent posterior task would remain at the last recovered lower amount unless the reviewed conditions justified more. Yue enjoyed the empty exercise more than expected. She corrected the stance, then looked at the inactive receiver without needing it to move.

kiln_p18_038.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_038.text: The ordinary source block for the month approached its agreed end. Tan brought the actual remaining allowance and the next quoted cost to the owner. Yue's wages and the funded teaching agreement covered different things; she wouldn't quietly draw practice charge from the commercial firing account. The renewed block preserved the planned recovered sessions and no additional private repetitions. Luo checked its compatible-source qualification before use. Yue had grown accustomed to this finite arrangement. Ambition still wanted more, but more had become an amount someone had to supply and a body someone had to recover, rather than a poetic instruction.

kiln_p18_039.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_039.text: She spent a quiet afternoon studying refinement loss. A larger admitted quantity could leave less usable compatible reserve if gathered carelessly and discharged later. Slower practice improved the fraction she could retain safely, but required time and ordinary rest. The approved method did not make loss disappear. Yue followed the measured process and stopped before fatigue changed the result. Her private page contained a useful reading and several unattractive costs. She kept them together. The eventual thirty-six-unit threshold would need to survive the sampling discharge and normal life, not merely appear before the apparatus had asked its first question.

kiln_p18_040.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_040.text: The cook asked why every teacher seemed to care about breakfast. Yue explained the next-day ordinary checks and discovered that she sounded like Luo. The cook smiled and gave her the regular portion. 'Good. You can become a great cultivator after the bowls are washed.' Yue offered to wash the lighter stack within her work clearance. Jian took the heavier ordinary tub under his permitted duty, while Zhu complained that all their wisdom had produced a laborious meal. The cook said wisdom rarely rinsed itself. They worked together until the kitchen looked less like the aftermath of a edible war.

kiln_p18_041.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_041.text: A district assessor's letter arrived with provisional dates for the four-pair examination. The assessor was independent of Luo's daily teaching and would use calibrated apparatus with a changed task order. The offered window didn't imply Yue was already ready. If reserve, purity or recovery failed, the appointment would shift rather than lower the method. She read the letter twice and felt both thrilled and irritated. Peng asked what she wanted entered in the schedule. Yue chose a preparation visit first, with no rank claim and no promised passing date. The assessor would meet the actual candidate, not a hopeful advertisement.

kiln_p18_042.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_042.text: Luo asked her to explain the whole method as if the assessor knew nothing of their friendship. She named four distinct primary pairs, the agreed post-sampling usable reserve and compatible fraction, separate quarter useful tasks, independent interruption, full release, actual rest and following-day movement checks. He interrupted when she called the posterior result stable without naming its repeated recovered days. She corrected the phrase. Her mouth was dry by the end. Then Luo said, 'I would trust that explanation with a person I have never met.' She took the page back and smiled at him.

kiln_p18_043.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_043.text: Yue asked whether he expected her to pass. He said he expected her to tell the truth. She groaned at the teacher's infuriating answer. He laughed, then said the actual route work looked promising, reserve and compatible fraction still needed to reach the agreed level, and the independent trials could reveal questions they had missed. He would be pleased if she passed and remain her teacher if she needed more time. That last sentence loosened something she had not known she was holding. The examination did not have to threaten the relationship in order to mean something.

kiln_p18_044.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_044.text: She wrote to her family with the actual progress: shoulder improving, ordinary work paid, posterior route begun, final four-pair assessment not yet earned. She crossed out a sentence that made the appointment sound like advancement. Her earlier travel letters had sometimes offered certainty because she wanted home to worry less. Now she described the bounded tasks and months more plainly. The letter felt less dazzling and more like her own life. She paid the ordinary postage from her wages and kept a copy. No messenger would turn the offered date into a rank her body had not yet established.

kiln_p18_045.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_045.text: Jian saw her sealing the letter and asked if honesty always made people anxious. Yue said sometimes it did, and sometimes a confident lie merely postponed anxiety into a harder place. He thought about his qualification promise and asked Peng to send a corrected household update with the current review course. His mother already knew the hearing, but a cousin still expected the old job date. He wrote the correction himself and left the hopeful future as hope. Yue helped him find the courier price, not the perfect sentence. Their two ordinary letters left on the same muddy cart.

kiln_p18_046.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_046.text: The communal kitchen's second body comparison passed the defined cleaning and temperature sequence without the earlier foot crack. Zhu still wanted an ordinary handling trial and a paid production plan before accepting the full commission. The owner agreed. They offered a prototype set under a clear trial arrangement, with feedback and inspection afterward. Yue packed the samples with the retained labels and copies. She hoped the kitchen would like them, then reminded herself that useful criticism would be worth the journey too. She left space in the packet for the washer's notes after the agreed trial.

kiln_p18_047.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_047.text: The caretaker returned the prototype feedback with an unexpected complaint: the bowls were sturdy and cleaned well, but one shape encouraged too much serving for the kitchen's actual meal budget. Zhu stared at the line, then laughed in dismay. Nobody had thought to ask how a generous bowl changed an ordinary portion. They made a smaller cold model and discussed the useful capacity with the caretaker and washer. Zhu corrected the capacity note. Yue enjoyed the discovery because it was neither dangerous nor trivial. The caretaker marked her preferred capacity on the cold model and returned it with thanks.

kiln_p18_048.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_048.text: Tan calculated the revised production proposal from the new capacity, actual body preparation and available firing space. The owner refused a discount based on imagined future orders. The kitchen could purchase a fair quantity under a staged agreement after the prototype inspection, and the hall could accept work it had time and material to perform. Yue listened while the proposed commission became smaller and clearer. Zhu would receive her agreed design share if accepted. Jian's supervised cold work would remain paid labor, not a heroic donation to redeem the incident. The bowl's modest shape seemed to have improved everyone's honesty.

kiln_p18_049.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_049.text: The hot afternoon ended with a thunderstorm beyond the hills, too far away to wet the yard. Yue watched the changing light from the safe window while her practice apparatus remained inactive. A storm could be beautiful without becoming a source she was qualified to capture. Zhu set a deep-blue tile beside her and asked whether the color now looked like evening. It did. The trimmer looked delighted, then added that the latest ordinary comparison still needed repetition. Yue raised a cup of ordinary water. Their unfinished achievements could share a toast without being promoted to completed methods.

kiln_p18_050.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_050.text: Luo returned to the archive after supper to inspect an old examiner's dispute. The case concerned a candidate who passed an apparatus task but concealed next-day numbness. His rank hadn't been confirmed after the recovered check exposed the problem. The record didn't predict Yue's future. It explained why the present method required following-day ordinary touch and movement rather than only a clever demonstration. Yue read the candidate's own correction and wondered what shame had made him hide the symptom. She wrote the reason for the next-day checks in her notes and went upstairs before fatigue turned the lesson into fear.

kiln_p18_051.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_051.text: On the next ordinary rest day she visited the river alone, choosing the safe bridge rather than the tempting boards. She ate a purchased bun under willow shade and let the uncharged water move at its own pace. Her ambition had become less loud without becoming smaller. She still wanted the fifth stage, still imagined the pleasure of a teacher writing it beside her name. She also wanted sound sleep, useful work and a body that could meet tomorrow without secretly borrowing from next month. The river offered no judgment. It gave her a cool place to finish lunch.

kiln_p18_052.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_052.text: When she returned, Zhu asked for help choosing between two blue tiles that differed only under slanting light. Yue chose one, then changed her mind when the cloud moved. The trimmer called her an independent assessor of weather. Jian proposed displaying both with the lighting note. Peng approved the ordinary record and threatened to make them all carry the exhibition table if they spent another hour debating a color no customer had yet ordered. They got to work. The hall was busy with unfinished things, and for once Yue found that abundance inviting enough to keep her at the table.

kiln_p18_053.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_053.text: The next posterior repetition took place after a recovered night and normal work checks. Quarter input over four breaths produced the eighth useful unit, then interrupted and released cleanly. Luo repeated the dry mixed naming exercise after actual rest, and Yue distinguished both leg pairs without hunting for the wrong outward contact. The following-day movement check remained normal, with no lingering calf sensation. Su Yan's reviewed method now allowed a first half-input attempt on a later recovered day, capped at an eighth per breath or any lower recovered limit. Yue wrote the permission beside the evidence that had earned it.

kiln_p18_054.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_054.text: That later day did not go perfectly. The first two breaths gathered correctly, but on the third Yue felt the posterior contact narrowing and interrupted before completing the planned half input. The actual admitted amount was recorded; the receiver had not produced the final useful quarter. Luo discharged to ground and gave her ordinary rest. She wanted to call the task almost successful. He asked which useful result almost had established. She crossed out the phrase before it entered the record. Zhu later told her almost-blue glaze had exactly the same commercial weakness, though it looked prettier on a tile.

kiln_p18_055.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_055.text: The next-day check found ordinary movement and touch normal. Luo returned to the last recovered quarter-input task rather than repeat the higher amount because the calendar had advanced. Yue completed the lower eighth-useful task cleanly and rested. She found the retreat difficult until Jian asked why a known safe result had become embarrassing. He didn't intend a clever accusation. The question came from his own weeks of cold repetition. She answered that she had wanted the fourth pair to feel like arrival. He said the first safe page after a wrong page had begun to feel like arrival to him.

kiln_p18_056.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_056.text: Her usable reserve approached thirty-two units after the usual sampling cost, while compatible charge remained under ninety percent. Slower gathering and refinement had improved the result without removing discharge loss or the need for ordinary sleep. Luo kept the finite source block and varied the recovered practice schedule within its agreement. The four-pair method needed usable capacity, not an impressive stored total measured before testing spent some of it. Yue copied the readings carefully and corrected a smudged digit from the retained measurement slate. She could not earn the difference between thirty-two and thirty-six by making the ink more confident.

kiln_p18_057.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_057.text: She sent Su Yan a full progress account, including the stopped half-input posterior attempt and the lower recovered task. The reply didn't demand bravery. It suggested a stance change after a dry comparison, no increase in input and a fresh ordinary movement check. Yue worked through the empty positions with Luo and discovered that she'd been protecting the old shoulder by turning her upper body slightly. That ordinary habit changed how she balanced the leg task. The clinician reviewed the posture adjustment within the cleared range. A healing injury could leave a movement memory after pain had stopped announcing it.

kiln_p18_058.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_058.text: With the corrected stance and a separate recovered day, the first full posterior half input spread across four ordinary breaths. No breath exceeded an eighth unit. The guarded receiver moved the quarter useful weight, and Yue interrupted cleanly during the independent stop comparison before complete grounded release. Luo recorded the result and made her rest before the arm check could be considered. She felt no dazzling flood through an imagined circuit. The new route was a distinct primary inward and outward pair, useful briefly at the agreed scale. She walked upstairs afterward carrying nothing heavier than her checked page.

kiln_p18_059.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_059.text: Her next-day touch, grip and leg movement were normal, including ordinary stairs within her cleared work. The result repeated on a later recovered day with the same bounded input and independent release. Yue had now demonstrated brief useful work through each of the four distinct primary pairs, but not the final reserve and purity thresholds or three independent formal trials. Luo said the completed new route deserved pleasure. She smiled before he finished. At supper Zhu presented the gray tile as an award for reaching almost-blue. Jian applauded with a clean spoon until Peng reminded him where supper utensils belonged.

kiln_p18_060.speaker: narrator
kiln_p18_060.text: On the final evening of the thirty-first week, Yue climbed the lodging stairs without thinking about each step. That absence of attention startled her more than the quarter-unit receiver had. Her body had recovered enough for many ordinary tasks, while sudden overhead catching remained outside clearance. The posterior record lay beside the anterior record, both bounded and genuine. She was still fourth stage. The next step would ask independent eyes to examine what her teachers already knew, and enough recovered reserve to make the useful work repeatable. Outside, the warm yard smelled of clay drying slowly under an honest schedule.
